item.title: Kill Goofy — Sun Oct 18, 1:30 PM — Grove Street Theater
item.description:
Apricot Sky Productions’s new play, Kill Goofy by Livingston playwright Eric Alter, opens October 9 and plays for three weekends throught October 25. The story is simple on the surface. Two best friends, inseparable at thirteen, haven’t spoken in thirty years. One of them never left his childhood bedroom. His mother never left because someone had to take care of him. Then the other one comes back to town, and everyone in that house has been keeping the same secret. It’s a play about the things we never say to the people closest to us, and it sends people out the door talking. Please note the play deals with difficult subject matter and is recommended for ages 15 and up. The full synopsis and content advisory plus more information are at https://apricotskyproductions.com/killgoofy. Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook

item.title: Cassandra: An Ongoing Tragedy, presented by Mosaic Dance Theater Company — Sun Oct 18, 3:00 PM — first congregation church
item.description:
Rich with emotional and social relevance, “Cassandra: An Ongoing Tragedy” by Ruth Cantrell contrasts Greek myths to modern day tragedies – war, terrorism, racism, sexual assault, gun violence, depicting the eternal existence of hate, and exploring the impact of the evils brought forth from Pandora’s Box. The stories in this piece are related by fictional characters in historical situations, through spoken word and dance, with an original score. Cast of 11. Oct 16 at 7pm, Oct 17 at 5pm, Oct 18 at 3pm. CONTENT WARNING This production shows graphic images of violence, including warfare, bombings, and their victims, with intense, jarring audio of gunfire and explosions. It is intended for mature audiences and those seeking to understand the events. Please take care of your well-being. Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook

item.title: Tuesday Night Open Studio Figure Drawing — Tue Oct 20, 7:00 PM — the Space
item.description:
Every Tuesday, 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space | All skill levels welcome *Cover art by Ling Chen.
Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. Each week a different model – usually nude, and sometimes clothed – serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say, observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. This has become a supportive community of seekers, artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. item.title: From Swastika to Jim Crow (2000): Screening and Discussion — Sun Nov 1, 2:00 PM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
Explore an influential, little-known chapter in the history of Black-Jewish relations in America. We'll be screening a documentary film, From Swastika to Jim Crow, based on a book by the same title by Gabrielle Simon Edgcomb. It tells the story of German-Jewish refugees, who, expelled from their homeland by Hitler and the Nazis, found new lives and careers at historically Black colleges and universities in the American South, influencing a whole generation of Black students and professionals. After the screening, Dr. Lillie Johnson Edwards and Rabbi Julie Roth, will discuss the film's significance. Dr. Edwards is a Drew University Professor Emerita of History and African American Studies. Rabbi Roth leads Congregation Shomrei Emunah of Montclair, NJ.
This program is co-sponsored by Shomrei Emunah (https://shomrei.org/) and The Mark Montclair https://themarkmtc.org).
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Montclair Film Festival - Kill. Bury. Print. — Sat Oct 17, 8:00 PM — The Wellmont Theater
item.description:
KILL. BURY. PRINT. tackles brazen corruption and press intimidation in remote southeast Oklahoma. When a small family-run newspaper begins reporting on allegations of sex, drugs, and violence within the county sheriff’s office, they find themselves the target of the sheriff’s retaliation. As tensions escalate, the paper secretly records the sheriff and local officials musing about killing and burying them, turning a local story into national news. Ben Klein’s film is a timely and powerful story of the relationship between journalists and those in power, a look at how corruption threatens our access to the truth. Q&A with Director Ben Klein and Producer Rachel Maddow follows the screening. Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook
